title: add jsonschema strict-mode: structured output validation and improved error messages (openai compat)
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: customers expect deterministic structured output and better compatibility with OpenAI's response_format/json_schema behaviors. This PR implements a strict-mode JSONSchema validator for the response_format API, improves error messages to surface validation failures in a developer-friendly way, and adds an OpenAI-compatibility layer for error codes and payload shapes.

Motivation: reduce production incidents where downstream consumers fail parsing model outputs. Strict mode enforces schema compliance: responses that do not validate are returned as structured error payloads (or rerouted to fallback models per routing policy). Non-strict mode remains unchanged.

Changes included (high-level): added JSONSchema validation pipeline in the runtime, plumbed response_format checks through the API layer, added a compatibility adapter to present errors in OpenAI-compatible shapes, extended SDKs and docs, and added integration tests.

Checklist: [x] Add validator and schema caching; [x] Wire into API request lifecycle; [x] Add OpenAI-compatible error payloads; [x] Add unit and integration tests; [x] Update docs and migration guide; [x] QA on Dedicated and Hosted.

Rollback plan: feature gated behind response_format.strict boolean and rollout flag. If we see increased errors, rollback by disabling strict flag via feature flag rollouts and revert adapter mapping.

Notes: description includes implementation notes, compatibility guarantees, and test plan. See linked Linear tasks for scope and acceptance criteria.

b9c3e1f: add response_format strict-mode flag to API surface and request validation path
c2d5f9a: openai compatibility adapter: map validation errors to openai error codes and message shapes
d3e9f0b: add python SDK helpers and docs examples for response_format.strict usage
e4f1a2c: integration tests for strict-mode end-to-end and fallback behavior

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Can we memoize compiled schemas per-model + schema-version? Implemented a schema_cache with LRU eviction in runtime/validation/schema_cache.go in commit b9c3e1f.

Liam O'Connor: Error messages look too verbose for end-users, suggest adding a short_code + full_detail fields. Implemented openai-compatible error payload with 'type', 'message', 'details' and 'full_message' in openai_compat_adapter.go.

Sofia Rivera: Add integration test for botched schema types (integer vs string). Added tests in tests/integration/jsonschema_strict_mode_test.py; CI originally failed on flakey test, reran and passed.
Maya Chen (author): Addressed comments and added docs + migration guide. Verified behavior on Dedicated internally and rolled out to a canary for Hosted API.
release_notes: Introduce response_format.strict (boolean). When true, responses are validated against provided JSONSchema; validation failures return structured OpenAI-compatible error payloads and can trigger fallback routing. Backwards compatible when not enabled.
notes_on_backwards_compatibility: Default behavior unchanged when response_format.strict is not set. SDK helpers are additive. OpenAI compatibility adapter only affects error payload shapes for validation failures and is behind the strict flag.
test_plan: Unit tests for validator, cache, and adapter. Integration tests with Hosted API canary (strict on for 5% traffic). Manual QA: sample prompts that slightly diverge from schema to validate error payload clarity. End-to-end tests included in CI.
motivation: Reduce parsing failures in downstream consumers and align Redwood's structured output semantics with developer expectations and OpenAI compatibility for strict validation error reporting.
